text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm proposing we onboard a new open model (ceres-14b) for hosted + dedicated + private. Main asks: run quantization experiments (8-bit and 4-bit), end-to-end eval vs our current prod model on conv/code benchmarks, and produce a deployment + canary/rollback checklist. target: <= 180ms p50 for short chat (<=256 tokens) on hosted, p95 < 600ms if possible; quality drop vs baseline < 2% on our eval suites.

jonathan: +1. Can you add expected throughput per GPU and memory needs? also priority (P1/P2)?

maya: P1 for hosted + dedicated (customers asked), P2 for private. Rough mem estimate: 28–38 GB FP16; with int8 we can aim for 16–20 GB; int4 experiments might fit in 12–16GB but will need AWQ/QLoRA tests. I'll have more after a quick compile pass.

lina: For experiments, let's follow a reproducible matrix:
- baseline: current-prod (prod-3b variant) evals (conv, code, safety).
- ceres FP16 (no quant) performance + quality.
- ceres bnb-8bit (bitsandbytes quant) quality/perf.
- ceres AWQ-int4 and/or GPTQ int4 runs (compare accuracy vs latency).
- compile with XLA/CUDA kernels + run BATCH sizes {1,4,8} and seq lenses {64,256,1024}.
Include seed/commit ids and exact finetune/responses so we can reproduce.

sam: For quality gating, propose these automated checks:
- unit evals: conv QA F1, code pass@1, and hallucination score. each must be within 2% of baseline or flagged.
- blackbox A/B: traffic-split for 48h with N=2k real requests, check KL divergence of token distrib and a pooled metric.
- human spot-check: 30 prompts for critical flows.
If any gating fails, we auto-fail canary and rollback.

product-ux: Ask: what will user-facing behavior be during canary? We need fallback plan so customers don't see lower-quality responses. Also add an opt-out for enterprise customers.

maya: Agreed. Plan: staged rollout with automatic fallback to ceres-7b (smaller family sibling) for failed requests or if QoS triggers. For enterprise, we'll default them to pinned model until we sign off.

lina: Draft rollout checklist (high level):
1) Intake form completed (owner, use case, data sensitivity, expected QPS).
2) Baseline run + regression report (automated).
3) Quantization matrix run (fp16, bnb8, awq4, gptq4) with perf numbers.
4) Compile & kernel selection report (list of kernels that mattered).
5) Staging deploy (internal traffic only) with tracing enabled.
6) Canary: hosted: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 2 days if metrics OK. dedicated: route 5% of sessions to new model on dedicated pool, ensure autoscaler margins. private: customer-specific plan + offline test.
7) Observability: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, eval metric drift, and top-10 prompt regression list.
8) Rollback triggers: quality drop >2% on key evals OR p95 latency >2x baseline OR error rate >0.5%.
9) Fallback route: automatic fallback to ceres-7b or last-stable model with seamless reroute and monotonic session IDs.
10) Postmortem and retention of eval artifacts.

sam: Additions for dedicated/private:
- capacity planning: estimate GPU-hours and reserve (H100 vs A100), consider multi-GPU sharding if memory >48GB.
- KMS/HSM notes for private: ensure model weights encrypted at rest for on-prem.
- Network egress: private VPC configs and allowlist for telemetry (if customer permits).

maya: Quick config snippet for our deploy tool (for ops):
```yaml
model: ceres-14b
variants:
  - name: ceres-14b-fp16
  - name: ceres-14b-bnb8
deployment:
  mode: hosted
  canary:
    steps:
      - percent: 5
        duration: 30m
      - percent: 20
        duration: 2h
      - percent: 50
        duration: 12h
  fallback_model: ceres-7b
  rollback_triggers:
    - eval_quality_drop_pct: 2
    - p95_latency_multiplier: 2
```

jonathan: Ops question: how do we handle model variant routing when capacity is constrained? e.g., if ceres-14b-bnb8 is out of slots, route to ceres-14b-fp16 or ceres-7b? We should define an ordered fallback policy.

lina: Suggested routing policy: primary -> ceres-14b-bnb8, secondary -> ceres-14b-fp16, tertiary -> ceres-7b (costly but safe). For dedicated customers who asked for isolation, primary should be the pinned variant per contract; we fallback to their pinned smaller variant not public fallback.

deploy-bot: deploy-checklist: canary flag present, metrics hooks configured, tracing=on, eval-webhook set, rollback webhook configured.

maya: Action items: 
- maya: run baseline + initial compile (ETA: 2 business days).
- lina: prepare quant matrix infra + pipeline (ETA: 3 days).
- sam: write automated gating rules into CI (ETA: 3 days).
- jonathan: capacity estimate + cost calc for dedicated (ETA: 4 days).
- product-ux: draft customer communication + opt-out UI (ETA: 5 days).
I'll update the thread with links to reproducible run artifacts. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

product-ux: please ping me for any user-facing wording, also will run risk review for hallucination-sensitive flows.

lina: leaving a note: remember to version evalsets and include seed / prompt templates in artifacts.

maya: noted — uploading staging config once first compile passes.

sam: sounds good. I'll start wiring the canary alerting now.

maya: end.
